subject: creative-arts-sp
description: Creative Arts Senior Phase (Grades 7–9). CAPS-aligned. Two of the four art forms are built — Music and Visual Arts (the two with rich tap-native theory). Dance and Drama are excluded as movement/performance-based. Each art form has three CAPS topics. All skills open once the grade is selected (gate NONE). Making/performing work is reframed into tap-only knowledge. No free text.

levels.title: Grade 7 — Creative Arts
levels.description: Grade 7 Creative Arts (CAPS Senior Phase). Two art forms — Music and Visual Arts — taught across the year. Dance and Drama are excluded (movement/performance-based, cannot be tapped).

atomic_skills.title: Note values and rests
atomic_skills.description: Reading and naming note values and their rests — semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver and the dotted minim — and how long each lasts.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Note values and rests".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A note's value tells you how many beats it lasts; a semibreve is longest, a quaver short.

atomic_skills.title: Treble and bass clef
atomic_skills.description: Naming notes on the lines and spaces of the treble and bass clefs.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Treble and bass clef".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The clef at the start of a staff tells you which note each line and space stands for.

atomic_skills.title: Beat and metre
atomic_skills.description: Hearing and counting the beat in duple (2), triple (3) and quadruple (4) time.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Beat and metre".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The metre is how the beats group — in 2s, 3s or 4s — and the first beat of each group is the strongest.

atomic_skills.title: Tonic sol-fa
atomic_skills.description: Using tonic sol-fa names (doh, re, mi…) to sight-sing simple melodic phrases.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Tonic sol-fa".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tonic sol-fa gives each note of the scale a name (doh re mi fa soh la ti doh) to help you sing it.

atomic_skills.title: Describing music
atomic_skills.description: Listening and describing a piece by its tempo (fast/slow), dynamics (soft/loud), metre and the mood or story it tells.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Describing music".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: When you describe music, listen for how fast (tempo), how loud (dynamics), the beat grouping and the mood.

atomic_skills.title: Instruments in a performance
atomic_skills.description: Recognising and naming common instruments heard in a performance.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Instruments in a performance".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Each instrument has its own sound; with practice you can pick out a drum, guitar or flute by ear.

atomic_skills.title: Creating music
atomic_skills.description: The building blocks of creating music — ostinato, riff, question-and-answer, melodic and rhythmic repetition, and graphic scores.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Creating music".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An ostinato or riff is a short pattern repeated; question-and-answer is one phrase 'answered' by another.

atomic_skills.title: Singing and song types
atomic_skills.description: Knowing the song types learners sing — the National Anthem, folk songs, rounds and part-songs — and accompanying with body percussion.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Singing and song types".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A round is a song where groups start at different times; body percussion is clapping, clicking or stamping a beat.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Art elements & design
tiers.description: CAPS G7 Visual Arts — Art elements & design.

atomic_skills.title: Art elements
atomic_skills.description: The art elements — line, shape, tone, texture and colour — and recognising them in artworks.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Art elements".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The art elements are the basic 'ingredients' of any artwork: line, shape, tone, texture and colour.

atomic_skills.title: Colour theory
atomic_skills.description: Mixing colour and using complementary colours (opposites) and monochromatic colour (shades of one colour).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Colour theory".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Complementary colours sit opposite on the colour wheel; monochromatic means tints and shades of one colour.

atomic_skills.title: Design principles
atomic_skills.description: The design principles — balance, contrast, pattern, proportion and emphasis — used to arrange an artwork.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Design principles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Design principles are the 'rules' for arranging elements: balance, contrast, pattern, proportion and emphasis.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Making in 2D & 3D
tiers.description: CAPS G7 Visual Arts — Making in 2D & 3D.

atomic_skills.title: Drawing and 2D media
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind 2D making — drawing (line, tone, texture, mark-making), painting (colour-mixing, brushwork), simple etching, lettering and pattern-making.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Drawing and 2D media".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Different media make different marks; mark-making, brushwork and etching are ways to create texture and tone.

atomic_skills.title: Making in 3D
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind 3D making — construction and modelling, plane/depth/perspective, materials and tools, good craftsmanship, safety and using recyclable materials.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Making in 3D".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 3D work uses depth and space; good craftsmanship means working neatly, safely and caring for the environment.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Visual literacy
tiers.description: CAPS G7 Visual Arts — Visual literacy.

atomic_skills.title: Looking and analysing
atomic_skills.description: Looking at and talking about artworks — buildings, still life, masks and groups of figures — and reading their symbolic language.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Looking and analysing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Analysing art means describing what you see using the art elements, and asking what its symbols might mean.

atomic_skills.title: The artist and research
atomic_skills.description: The role of the artist in their own society as contributor and observer, and beginning to research art.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The artist and research".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Artists contribute to and observe society; researching means gathering information and images about art.

levels.title: Grade 8 — Creative Arts
levels.description: Grade 8 Creative Arts (CAPS Senior Phase). Two art forms — Music and Visual Arts — taught across the year. Dance and Drama are excluded (movement/performance-based, cannot be tapped).

atomic_skills.title: Duration and metre
atomic_skills.description: Reading rhythm in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 and compound duple 6/8 time.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Duration and metre".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The top number of a time signature counts beats in a bar; 6/8 groups six quavers into two main beats.

atomic_skills.title: Major scales
atomic_skills.description: Building the major scales of C, G, D and F major using tones and semitones.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Major scales".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A major scale follows the pattern tone-tone-semitone-tone-tone-tone-semitone from its starting note.

atomic_skills.title: Reading in keys
atomic_skills.description: Reading (singing or playing) music in the keys of C, G, D and F major.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Reading in keys".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The key tells you which sharps or flats to use throughout the piece.

atomic_skills.title: Music terminology
atomic_skills.description: Musical terms for tempo (moderato, presto, ritardando, a tempo) and articulation (legato, staccato).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Music terminology".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tempo terms tell you the speed (presto = fast); articulation tells you how to play notes (staccato = short, detached).

atomic_skills.title: Elements across styles
atomic_skills.description: Identifying the elements and principles of music — metre, dynamics, repetition, contrast — across Western classical, African, Indian and popular styles.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Elements across styles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Every style uses the same elements — metre, dynamics, repetition, contrast — but in its own way.

atomic_skills.title: Instrument families
atomic_skills.description: Grouping instruments by how they make sound — chordophones (strings), idiophones, membranophones (drums) and aerophones (wind).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Instrument families".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Instruments group by how sound is made: chordophones (strings), membranophones (skins), idiophones (the body itself), aerophones (air).

atomic_skills.title: Creating and composing
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind composing — building a piece with structure and combining music with another art form.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Creating and composing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Composing means making your own music with a clear structure; it can be combined with dance, drama or art.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Art elements & design
tiers.description: CAPS G8 Visual Arts — Art elements & design.

atomic_skills.title: Art elements and analogous colour
atomic_skills.description: The art elements again, now adding analogous (related, neighbouring) colour.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Art elements and analogous colour".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Analogous colours sit next to each other on the colour wheel, like blue, blue-green and green.

atomic_skills.title: Design principles
atomic_skills.description: Using the design principles with greater control to plan and arrange artworks.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Design principles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Design principles — balance, contrast, pattern, proportion, emphasis — guide how you arrange an artwork.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Making in 2D & 3D
tiers.description: CAPS G8 Visual Arts — Making in 2D & 3D.

atomic_skills.title: Drawing, painting and media
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind extended 2D making — drawing and painting with a wider range of media and techniques, lettering, pattern and paper size/format.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Drawing, painting and media".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Trying different media, scales and formats widens what your drawing and painting can express.

atomic_skills.title: Making in 3D
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind more complex 3D making — construction and modelling, manipulating materials and tools with good craftsmanship and safety, recyclable materials, and themes from the social world.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Making in 3D".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: More complex 3D work deepens spatial awareness; good craftsmanship, safety and recycling still matter.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Visual literacy
tiers.description: CAPS G8 Visual Arts — Visual literacy.

atomic_skills.title: Looking and analysing
atomic_skills.description: Analysing artworks and design — creative lettering and functional containers — and exploring careers in fashion design.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Looking and analysing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Reading design means asking how something looks AND how it works; many careers, like fashion, blend both.

atomic_skills.title: The artist, research and planning
atomic_skills.description: The role of the artist in the wider society and arts careers, developing research skills, and planning and preparing for a project.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The artist, research and planning".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Planning a project means collecting resources, references and rough sketches before the final work.

levels.title: Grade 9 — Creative Arts
levels.description: Grade 9 Creative Arts (CAPS Senior Phase). Two art forms — Music and Visual Arts — taught across the year. Dance and Drama are excluded (movement/performance-based, cannot be tapped).

atomic_skills.title: Scales in treble and bass clef
atomic_skills.description: Writing the scales of C, G, D and F major in both the treble and bass clefs.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Scales in treble and bass clef".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The same scale can be written in either clef — the note names are the same, the staff position differs.

atomic_skills.title: Key signatures
atomic_skills.description: The key signatures of C, G, D and F major and the sharps they use.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Key signatures".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A key signature lists the sharps or flats for a key: C has none, G has F#, D has F# and C#, F has B flat.

atomic_skills.title: Ledger lines
atomic_skills.description: Reading notes on ledger lines — the short lines above and below the staff.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Ledger lines".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ledger lines extend the staff so you can write notes that are too high or too low to fit on it.

atomic_skills.title: Intervals
atomic_skills.description: Naming the distance between two notes — the interval — by counting note names.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Intervals".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An interval is counted by including both notes: C up to G is a 5th (C-D-E-F-G).

atomic_skills.title: Triads
atomic_skills.description: Building a triad — a three-note chord of a root, third and fifth.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Triads".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A triad stacks three notes a third apart: the root, the note two letters up, and the note four letters up.

atomic_skills.title: Writing scales rhythmically
atomic_skills.description: Writing the C, G, D and F major scales using the note values learnt.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Writing scales rhythmically".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Writing a scale rhythmically combines the right pitches with chosen note values in a bar.

atomic_skills.title: Orchestral families
atomic_skills.description: The four families of the orchestra — strings, woodwind, brass and percussion — and how each produces sound.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Orchestral families".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The orchestra groups instruments into strings, woodwind, brass and percussion by how they make their sound.

atomic_skills.title: Music styles
atomic_skills.description: The features of popular styles — reggae, kwaito, R&B and African jazz — including rhythm, tempo, instruments and voices.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Music styles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Each style has signature features; kwaito is slow South African house, reggae has its off-beat rhythm.

atomic_skills.title: Musicals, opera and the anthem
atomic_skills.description: Listening to a musical or opera (such as West Side Story or The Magic Flute), following its storyline, and discussing the National Anthem.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Musicals, opera and the anthem".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A musical or opera tells a story through song; the South African anthem joins five languages and two melodies.

atomic_skills.title: Composing
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind Grade 9 composing — completing a four-bar phrase, adding music to words, and creating an advertisement jingle.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Composing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Completing a phrase means writing an 'answer' that balances the opening; a jingle is a short, catchy advert tune.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Art elements & design
tiers.description: CAPS G9 Visual Arts — Art elements & design.

atomic_skills.title: Art elements and analogous colour
atomic_skills.description: The art elements with a global focus, using analogous and related colour with control.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Art elements and analogous colour".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Analogous colours (neighbours on the wheel) create harmony; the elements stay the building blocks of art.

atomic_skills.title: Design principles
atomic_skills.description: Applying the design principles independently to plan and judge artworks.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Design principles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: By Grade 9 you use balance, contrast, pattern, proportion and emphasis to plan and critique work yourself.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Making in 2D & 3D
tiers.description: CAPS G9 Visual Arts — Making in 2D & 3D.

atomic_skills.title: Making in 2D and 3D
atomic_skills.description: Knowledge behind global-themed making — drawing, painting and etching, and personalised 3D construction and modelling with complex materials, craftsmanship and safety.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Making in 2D and 3D".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Personalised making lets you choose materials and techniques to express your own idea, made well and safely.

tiers.title: Visual Arts · Visual literacy
tiers.description: CAPS G9 Visual Arts — Visual literacy.

atomic_skills.title: Looking and analysing
atomic_skills.description: Analysing portraits, social commentary, popular culture and design in public spaces.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Looking and analysing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Art can comment on society; a portrait, poster or mural can carry a message as well as a likeness.

atomic_skills.title: The artist as social commentator
atomic_skills.description: The role of the artist as contributor, observer and social commentator in global society, working independently to research and plan.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The artist as social commentator".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A social commentator uses art to raise issues; by Grade 9 you research and plan your projects on your own.
